technique.how: Auscultate the apex and left sternal border in a quiet room, comparing the intensity of S1/S2 with what is expected for the patient's habitus and, if possible, with earlier examinations; note whether the apex beat is impalpable. Pair with JVP and blood pressure/pulsus paradoxus.
technique.prerequisites: Quiet environment; knowledge of habitus, chest-wall thickness and known COPD/hyperinflation.

interpretation.positive_finding: Diminished heart sounds with a large effusion suggest tamponade physiology only in combination with elevated JVP, hypotension and pulsus paradoxus; alone they were present in roughly one-third of a medical tamponade series (sensitivity about 34%) and are common in COPD, obesity and pleural effusion.
interpretation.negative_finding: Normal heart sounds do not exclude tamponade: most patients in the largest medical series had audible heart sounds, and Beck triad is complete in only a minority.
interpretation.pitfalls: Hyperinflation (COPD), obesity, left pleural effusion and a noisy room all muffle heart sounds; conversely a small effusion can cause tamponade with normal sounds. Do not wait for the full Beck triad.
interpretation.changes_what: Muffled sounds + raised JVP + hypotension or pulsus >10 mmHg: immediate POCUS for effusion/tamponade. Muffled sounds alone: look for COPD/obesity/effusion; do not use to exclude tamponade.

estimates.target_condition: Cardiac tamponade (sensitivity only; no non-tamponade comparator); finding = diminished heart sounds
estimates.population: 56 medical patients with cardiac tamponade, single-centre case series, University of Cincinnati (malignancy 18, idiopathic pericarditis 8, uraemia 5)
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical/haemodynamic diagnosis of tamponade relieved by pericardiocentesis or pericardial resection
estimates.computed_from: 19 of 56 patients with diminished heart sounds: 19/56 = 0.339. Denominator assumed to be the whole series; the abstract does not state how many had heart sounds documented.
estimates.quote: We reviewed the cases of 56 medical patients wih cardiac tamponade … heart sounds were diminished in 19 patients

estimates.target_condition: Cardiac tamponade (sensitivity only; mostly tuberculous, n = 15); finding = decreased intensity of heart sounds
estimates.population: 15 prospectively studied patients with cardiac tamponade, cardiology department, University Hospital of Dakar, Senegal, 1999; mean age 33
estimates.reference_standard: Echocardiographic pericardial effusion with clinical tamponade treated by pericardiocentesis/drainage
estimates.quote: The clinical findings are: class III or IV NYHA dyspnea (86.6 %), pulsus paradoxus (66.6 %), and decrease intensity of the heart sounds (100 %).

sources.citation: Guberman BA, Fowler NO, Engel PJ, Gueron M, Allen JM. Cardiac tamponade in medical patients. Circulation. 1981.
Diao M, Ka TA, Kane A, Thiam O, Diop IB, Sarr M, Ba SA, Diouf SM. [Cardiac tamponade. Clinical, paraclinical, outcome, and therapeutic features. Report of 15 cases]. Dakar Med. 2005.
Roy CL, Minor MA, Brookhart MA, Choudhry NK. Does this patient with a pericardial effusion have cardiac tamponade? JAMA. 2007.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use audible heart sounds to exclude tamponade, and do not treat muffled sounds as tamponade in a COPD or obese patient without JVP/BP/pulsus or ultrasound corroboration.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Suspected tamponade (effusion with hypotension, raised JVP or pulsus paradoxus >10 mmHg) needs immediate echocardiography and cardiology for pericardiocentesis; do not delay for the complete Beck triad.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No interobserver data for heart-sound intensity located; the sign is subjective and habitus-dependent.

extraction_notes: Both estimates are sensitivity-only from tamponade case series (no non-tamponade comparator), hence partially_quantified and no LR. Guberman 1981 sensitivity is computed from '19 patients' over the series total of 56 (denominator assumption stated in computed_from); the same abstract notes "most patients did not have a small quiet heart, and blood pressure was often well maintained" (Abstract). Diao 2005 is a small (n = 15), mostly tuberculous series in Senegal, so 100% is an upper bound with wide uncertainty and different case mix. Roy 2007 RCE (PMID 17456823) is cited as the pooled reference; it is not in PMC and its abstract does not list diminished heart sounds, so its pooled sensitivity (unverified recall: ~28%) is not entered. Search 'cardiac tamponade clinical signs heart sounds pulsus paradoxus prospective' returned only Diao 2005.
